_comment: Token prices in $/MTok, per provider. usage-report.py reads this file; editing it changes the report without touching the parser. A family key matches by substring against the model name, longest key first, so 'gpt-5.4-mini' wins over 'gpt-5.4'. cache_write_multiplier and cache_read_multiplier are applied to the input price. Set rates_verified to false for a provider whose numbers you have not checked against the vendor's current price list — the report then labels its cost column as an estimate instead of presenting a guess as a fact.

codex._rates_note: OpenAI's Standard short-context rates from developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, checked 2026-09-26. Cached input is 0.1x the input price for every model listed; cache writes are 1.25x for the gpt-6 and gpt-5.6 models, and the page says cache-write pricing does not apply to gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.3-codex (Codex records no cache-write tokens for them, so the 1.25x never bills there). A model name matching no family is priced as default_family (gpt-5.6-sol) — for an unreleased gpt-5.6 variant that may overstate the cost. Not modelled: long-context rates (input past 272K; no Codex call on record has come near it), Batch/Flex/Fast-mode tiers, the 10% data-residency uplift. gpt-5.6-sol is promotional pricing, available at least through 2026-11-21 — re-check after that date. codex-auto-review is Codex's internal review model and is not on the price list; it is priced as gpt-5.6-terra, an assumption.
